articles.title: Generative Modeling: Learning the Distribution Behind the Data
articles.excerpt: Generative Modeling starts with a simple shift in perspective: instead of memorizing individual observations, learn the probabilistic structure that produced them. If a model can represent that struct…
articles.body: Generative Modeling starts with a simple shift in perspective: instead of memorizing individual observations, learn the probabilistic structure that produced them. If a model can represent that structure, it can use the learned distribution to evaluate data and generate new samples that follow the same underlying patterns. That gives us the core mental model: Learn the distribution behind the data, then use that distribution for estimation or generation. From Observed Data to a Model Distribution Suppose a dataset contains many dog images. Storing those images is not enough to create a new dog image that was never part of the training set.

articles.title: Fixing WSL 2.7.x `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` After an Update
articles.excerpt: Overview If you recently updated WSL to version 2.7.x and your distro suddenly fails to start with ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND, this article walks through how I diagnosed and fixed the problem. To save you t…
articles.body: Overview If you recently updated WSL to version 2.7.x and your distro suddenly fails to start with ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND , this article walks through how I diagnosed and fixed the problem. Spoiler To save you time, here is the root cause of the error before we dive into the step-by-step fix. WSL relies on files installed under C:\Program Files\WSL . In this case, the WSL installation was missing system.vhd . The WSL VM therefore could not start because Hyper-V was instructed to attach a virtual disk that did not exist. How I Fixed WSL 2.7.x ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND Before we start, let's get this out of the way: Important: This procedure repairs the WSL installation files; it does not unregister or delete your existing distributions.

articles.excerpt: It turns out, I got the timeline wrong. The first bit of work I did on Packet Sender was to test light mode. See, Dan Nagle, creator and maintainer of Packet Sender, had implemented light and dark mod…
articles.body: It turns out, I got the timeline wrong. The first bit of work I did on Packet Sender was to test light mode. See, Dan Nagle, creator and maintainer of Packet Sender, had implemented light and dark mode. But he only uses dark mode personally. Because of this, he missed the fact that some parts of the dark mode theme was hanging on after the app switched to light mode. Having fixed the bug, he wanted me to manually test the app going through as much UI as possible to make sure that going from dark mode to light mode 100% converted the app to light mode. I did not know this until quite recently, but it turns out that there is a setting you can toggle. I thought Packet Sender followed whatever the operating system is set to; that turned out to be the truth but not the whole truth. Whut?

articles.title: MLOps for Developers: Deploying, Monitoring, and Optimizing Machine Learning Models
articles.excerpt: How to deploy, monitor, and optimize ML models in production: GPU selection, VRAM requirements, cloud vs local cost, model drift, and CI/CD pipelines for ML In 2020, a team at a financial services com…
articles.body: How to deploy, monitor, and optimize ML models in production: GPU selection, VRAM requirements, cloud vs local cost, model drift, and CI/CD pipelines for ML The Model That Worked in Jupyter and Failed in Production In 2020, a team at a financial services company trained a fraud detection model that achieved 99.2% accuracy in their Jupyter notebooks. They deployed it to production. Within a week, false positives had increased by 300%, and the company was blocking legitimate transactions from thousands of customers. The model wasn't broken — the data had changed. The pandemic had shifted spending patterns so dramatically that the model's training data no longer resembled reality. This is the central lesson of MLOps: a model is not a feature you ship once.

articles.excerpt: Putting privacy on a pedestal — if you can afford it.
articles.body: TL;DR UGREEN is launching three smart home hubs that combine network storage, video recording, and local AI processing. Instead of talking to Gemini in the cloud like you do with Google Home, here all voice commands are processed by the hub itself. Depending on your needs, UGREEN’s hardware can offer some seriously heavy-duty NVIDIA AI silicon. Smart homes are getting smarter, and that might just be a problem. While the idea of a more feature-reach, accessible, and proactive smart home sounds great on face value, the growing reliance of so many of these systems on cloud-based AI is making some shoppers think twice. UGREEN believes it might just have the solution in the form of some advanced smart home hubs.

articles.excerpt: UGREEN is hitting the ground running with a full slate of smart home devices.
articles.body: TL;DR UGREEN’s big smart home push involves the launch of a smart speaker, photo frame, and multiple cameras. The outdoor cameras are designed to work perfectly with the company’s new local-AI smart home hubs, and include both wired and solar-powered options. A smart speaker also makes it easy to connect with the company’s Uliya digital assistant. In addition to its pricey new smart home hubs , UGREEN is getting its smart home ambitions up to speed with a slate of its own hardware, including a speaker, photo frame, and trio of cameras. We’re looking at one indoor camera and two mountable outdoor cameras: the SynCare Indoor Cam ID500 Pro, SynCare PoE CAM OD600 Pro, and SynCare Battery Cam OD800 Pro. All three offer an 8MP, 4K main camera.

articles.title: UGREEN’s new Qi2 power bank has cooling you can see, as well as feel
articles.excerpt: Check out all the new additions to UGREEN's power solutions.
articles.body: TL;DR UGREEN’s got a bunch of new power solutions debuting, including the first Qi2 magnetic bank with liquid cooling. That’s joined by a set of new 2-in-1 and 3-in-1 chargers ideal for Apple users. Those combo chargers are available in both foldable travel sizes, as well as desktop stands. These days, power solutions aren’t just about capacity and speed. In order to reach the demanding limits we insist upon, more and more often manufacturers must contend with the ever-present specter of heat — not a battery’s best friend. And while we’ve seen plenty of ways to manage heat , you’ve probably never seen any quite like UGREEN’s latest — literally. Plenty of us already know and love the convenience of magnetic Qi2 battery banks , ready to pop right on the back of compatible phones and cases.

articles.title: 2 spacecraft will soon reach Mercury after 8 years in space. Here's what BepiColombo can do
articles.excerpt: After an 8-year trek to Mercury, BepiColombo will finally split into two spacecraft ready to track down the secrets of the least-explored planet in the inner solar system.
articles.body: Mercury, the tiniest and least-explored planet in the inner solar system, is hiding mysteries far larger than itself — and finally, scientists will soon be getting not one but two spacecraft designed to decode the strange world. That's thanks to the BepiColombo mission, a joint project of the European Space Agency (ESA) and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) that launched in October 2018. After a harrowing journey through the inner solar system, the mission is tackling a crucial maneuver on Thursday (Sept. 3) : separating its science equipment from the transport that carried it all that way.
articles.author: Meghan Bartels

articles.title: NASA to Cover Progress 96 Spacecraft Launch, Docking
articles.excerpt: NASA will provide live coverage of the launch and docking of a Roscosmos cargo spacecraft carrying about three tons of food, fuel, and supplies for the crew aboard the International Space Station. The…
articles.body: The Roscosmos Progress 92 cargo spacecraft is photographed in March 2026 from the International Space Station as it flies into an orbital sunset 267 miles above Earth’s surface. Credit: NASA NASA will provide live coverage of the launch and docking of a Roscosmos cargo spacecraft carrying about three tons of food, fuel, and supplies for the crew aboard the International Space Station. The unpiloted Progress 96 resupply spacecraft is scheduled to launch at 12:15 p.m. EDT (9:15 p.m. Baikonur time), Wednesday, Sept. 9, on a Soyuz rocket from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. NASA’s live launch coverage will begin at 12 p.m. After a two-day trip to the space station, Progress will dock autonomously to the Poisk module’s space-facing port at 2:37 p.m., Friday, Sept. 11.

articles.title: 'Strange New Worlds'' latest episode is a soap opera spoof, but hasn't 'Star Trek' always been a soap opera in space?
articles.excerpt: The latest 'Strange New Worlds' takes the silliness to warp factor nine, but soap opera plots have long been part of the 'Star Trek' mix
articles.body: "Strange New Worlds"' fourth season has doubled down on the show's long-established penchant for seeking out new genres beyond "Trek"'s traditional frontiers . So far the Enterprise has encountered Martians , hangovers and Muppets , and now its latest mission, "Like Chronitons Through the Hourglass", has made a detour into full-on soap opera territory. Thanks to the meddling of Q junior Trelane (Rhys Darby), the ship's lighting is slightly off, day-to-day operations are punctuated by ad breaks, and the crew has developed a tendency to stare wistfully into the middle distance. Reminders that Starfleet's finest are living out their very own "Days of Our Lives"-style TV show are everywhere, but — for all the deliberate overacting and pauses. In. All the. Wrong.

articles.title: 'A new mission starting today': 8 years after launch, BepiColombo begins Mercury arrival
articles.excerpt: After nearly eight years traveling through the inner solar system, the trailblazing BepiColombo spacecraft has finally begun its arrival at Mercury.
articles.body: After nearly eight years traveling through the inner solar system, the trailblazing BepiColombo spacecraft has finally begun its arrival at Mercury. The joint European Space Agency (ESA)-Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) mission reached a major milestone today (Sep. 3), entering its arrival phase at one of our sun's least-studied planets. BepiColombo's Mercury Transfer Module (MTM), the main power and propulsion system that has ferried a dual stack of planetary probes through space for nearly eight years, released its payload to kick off a sequence of operations that will ultimately place the two spacecraft in Mercury's orbit.
